title: Refresh Texture
content: ### **Objective** Edit texture images with an image editing tool (Photoshop, Illustrator…) and save over the original image with the same name and file location, press **Refresh** button to instantly apply the changes of the Fabric's texture images. **Location** Main Menu ▶ 3D/2D Window Background Right-click Pop-up Menu ▶ **Refresh Textures**
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to guide users on how to edit and instantly refresh fabric texture images in their 3D/2D projects using image editing tools.

title: Edit Texture Size (Property Editor)
content: ### **Objective** Use the Property Editor to resize the texture applied to the Patterns. ** Location** Object Browser ▶ Fabric Tab ▶ Fabric (Select the Desired One) ▶ **Property Editor** ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Fabric Tab ▶ Fabric (Select the Desired One) ▶ **Property Editor** → The selected Fabric's properties appear in the Property Editor. 2. Find the **Transformation** option which only appears [when a texture is applied to a Pattern.](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000471388-%EC%9B%90%EB%8B%A8-%ED%85%8D%EC%8A%A4%EC%B2%98-%EB%84%A3%EA%B8%B0) **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Angle** | Type in the rotating angle. **Width** | Set the texture width. **% (ver5.0.0)** | Configure the texture width with percentage. **Height** | Set the texture height. **% (ver5.0.0)** | Configure the texture height with percentage. **Lock Aspect Ratio** | Lock the width and height ratio.
content_description: This webpage provides a step-by-step guide for using the Property Editor to resize textures applied to patterns in the Fabric Tab of the Object Browser.

title: Unified Map 6.1
content: **Objective** When a pattern construction constrains a print layout, apply the texture using Unified Map. **Location** Object Browser ▶ Fabric Tab ▶ On the right button of Fabric Item **Texture Repeat / Unified Map**. Object Browser ▶ Fabric Tab ▶ Fabric Property Editor ▶ Material ▶**Texture Mapping** **Operation** 1. Click the tool/ menu indicated. 2. Use Unified Map to apply the texture differently. 3. Set the specific options of the Unified Map. Repeat U | Set the range for the image to be arranged between 0-1 in the U direction. ---|--- Repeat V | Set the range for the image to be arranged between 0-1 in the V direction. **※Note:** Once you have applied the Unified Fabric Map, the Edit Texture Tool will only rotate the Grain-line, NOT the Texture.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for applying texture to print layouts using the Unified Map feature in the Fabric Tab of the Object Browser.

title: Import AxF file
content: ### Objective Express textures by using the AxF file of X-Rite that express realistic fabric materials with various maps extracted by three-dimensional scanning of fabric. **Location** Object Browser ▶ **Fabric** **Operation** 1. Click the tool/ menu indicated in Location. ** ** 2. Right click the fabric item and **Import/ Import (Add).** → **Open File** window appears. 3. Select the AxF file and click **Open**. → Fabric property is converted into the property of AxF file. → When using **Import (Add)** , the properties that have already set are retained, only the properties that are not present are changed to the corresponding Axf file. (Ex: When having texture only, the other maps are applied such as Normal, Alpha, or etc) **※ Note:** You can drag and drop the AxF file to **Fabric** in **Object Browser** , 2D Pattern, and 3D Garment.
content_description: This web page provides a concise guide on importing and applying X-Rite's AxF files to enhance fabric textures with realistic properties and maps derived from 3D scans.

title: Adjust Density
content: **Objective** Use this function to express the weight ratio per unit (m²). The higher the value, the heavier the fabric. ### **Location** Object Browser ▶ Fabric Property Editor ▶ Physical Property ▶ Detail ▶ **Density** ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005704387/__.png)
content_description: This web page provides a tool for calculating the weight ratio per square meter of fabric, with higher values indicating heavier materials.

title: Apply Texture
content: **List of Contents** Apply Texture Add Texture Apply with Desired Map Type **Apply Texture **\- Apply an image file to the Fabric style to express fabric’s texture. \- Select a Fabric style from the Fabric tab under the Object Browser. Then, navigate to the Property Editor ▶ Material **▶ Texture.** ** Add Texture ** * **Via Property Editor** \- Select a Fabric style from the Fabric tab under the Object Browser. \- Click the Browser button next to the Texture option. \- The chosen image is applied as texture. * **Via Drag &Drop** \- From the PC’s Browser window, click, drag and drop the image file to the Browse button next to the Texture option. The image file is applied as texture. **Apply with Desired Map Type ** \- From the PC’s Browser window, drag and drop an image file to an object where the image should be applied to. \- The **Texture Map** Type window appears. Choose the desired Map type and select OK. **※ Note:** Normal and Roughness map are retained even if the texture is deleted. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: Explore how to effectively apply and customize textures to fabric styles using various methods in our comprehensive guide.

title: Specular Color
content: **List of Contents** Specular Color Apply Specular Color Adjust Shininess **Specular Color ** \- The **Specular Color** is the color of the light directly reflected from the fabric used to express glossy materials such as enamel. ** Apply Specular Color** \- Select the fabric item from the Object Browser. \- Navigate to the Property Editor and select the color chip next to the Material ▶**Specular Color.** \- When the color window appears, select the desired Specular Color. \- Brighter the Specular Color is, glossier the fabric will become. **Adjust Shininess** \- Select the fabric item from the Object Browser. \- Navigate to the Property Editor and expand the Material ▶ **Specular Color** to see its child menus. Locate the **Shininess** option. \- Move the scroll bar to adjust the gloss of the fabric. Higher the Shininess value is, glossier the fabric will become, like enamel. However, on the contrast, lower the Shininess value is, more regularly the gloss will spread on the surface of the fabric, like lame. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on applying specular color and adjusting shininess for fabric materials to achieve desired glossy effects.

title: Vizoo File Compatibility
content: ### Objective CLO is compatible with Vizoo 3D which scans actual material information (Color/Specular/Normal Map). **Location** Object Browser ▶ **Fabric Tab** **Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ **Fabric Tab** ** ** 2. Right-click on a Fabric style. 3. Select **Import xTex File** from the menu and load the relevant xTex file.
content_description: This webpage provides a step-by-step guide for importing xTex files into the Fabric Tab of the Object Browser in CLO, ensuring compatibility with Vizoo 3D material scanning.

title: Adjust Internal Damping
content: ### **Objective** Use this function to set resistance against the bouncing speed of Garments. Increasing the Internal Damping value is going to cause the Garment to slow down as if it is in underwater, and lowering the value is going to cause it to bounce very quickly. **※ Note:** Adjusting the measurement while putting Garments on does not make a noticeable difference therefore it is better to use during animation as it influences Garments when they are moving. **Location** Object Browser ▶ Fabric Property Editor ▶ Physical Property ▶ Detail ▶ **Internal Damping**
content_description: This web page provides guidance on adjusting the Internal Damping setting to control the bouncing speed of garments during animation for more realistic movement.

title: Topstitch Face Setting
content: ### **Objective** Select the face of Topstitch. ** Location** Object Browser ▶ Topstitch ▶ Topstitch Property Editor ▶ **Face** ** Explanation** ![30_Front.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115005622567/30_Front.png) | Topstitch is only set for the front of the Fabric. ---|--- ![30_Back.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115005674588/30_Back.png) | Topstitch is only set for the back of the Fabric. ![30_Both.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115005674608/30_Both.png) | Topstitch is set for the both sides of the Fabric. **** ※Note: Topstitch placed on the back of the Fabric do not appear in the 2D window (ver4.2.0).

title: Fabric_Normal Map
content: **Normal Map ** * **Normal Map ** \- Apply Normal Map images to express uneven texture more realistically. * **Adjust Intensity -**Select the fabric item from the Object Browser. \- Navigate to the Property Editor and expand the Material ▶ Texture to see its child menus. Then, expand the **Normal Map** option as well. \- Adjust the intensity of the Normal Map using the **Intensity** option. \- When the Normal Map Intensity values is adjusted from 0, CLO will automatically create a Normal Map and express the texture more realistically. * **Apply Normal Map Images ** * **Via Property Editor** \- The custom made Normal Maps can be applied to the fabric items as well. \- Select the fabric item from the Object Browser. \- Navigate to the Property Editor and expand the Material ▶**** Texture to see its child Menus. \- Click the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022233407/mceclip0.png)icon next to the Normal Map. The Open File browser will appear. \- Locate the desired Normal Map image and click Open. \- Adjust the intensity values to express the texture more realistically. * **Via Drag & Drop \- **From the PC’s Browser window, drag and drop a Normal Map image to the Browser button next to the Normal Map option. * **Apply with Desired Map Type ****-** From the PC’s Browser window, drag and drop an image file to an object where the image should be applied to. \- The Texture Map Type window appears. Choose the desired Map type and select OK. * Save Auto-generated Normal Map \- Normal Map generated when adjusting Intensity can now be saved. \- Adjust the Intensity under the Normal Map option. \- Navigate to Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Save as ▶Surface Textures and locate the saving path. \- Select Original size or Crop size when saving. \- The Normal Map can be saved when exporting as OBJ,FBX,LXO. **※** Note: Normal Map and Roughness Map are retained even if Texture is deleted.(ver.4.2)
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on how to apply and adjust normal map images to enhance the realistic texture of fabric items in CLO software.

title: Texture Generator (ver 7.1)
content: **List of Contents** **Open Texture ** **Select Area of Texture** **Set Options** **Save Texture Image** **Apply Texture** **Objective** Seamlessly generate texture maps with scanned or captured images, and check the results in real-time within the 3D window. **Location**** ** Object Browser ▶ Fabric ▶ ![mceclip0.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/13169546878617) Texture Generator **Operation ** **Open Texture** 1. Click the tool/menu indicated. → Texture Generator Opens. 2. Click Open at the left bottom of Texture Generator to open the texture image. → The size and resolution of the textures loaded are displayed at the top. → For XTEX files, other maps (Normal map, Opacity map etc.) in the folder are automatically loaded. **Select Area of Texture** 1. Find and click on the minimum area where the fabric pattern repeats. ▶ Drag to select. → The optimized result analyzed within the selected area will show up. → The analyzed result is repeated in the preview window at the bottom. 2. To adjust the area, move the point of the selected area. → It is analyzed automatically again within the selected area. 3. To maintain the selected area, click Manual at the right bottom of the selected area. → The selected area is maintained and repeated. **Set Options** The options below can be set only in Auto mode since they work based on the analyzed results. * **Fabric Type ** Select fabric type for more accurate analysis. The analysis is based on Normal Map, thus it is only vaild with the existence of Normal Map. \- Plain: Solid fabric without repeated patterns. \- Repeat Pattern: Fabric pattern is regular. \- Random Color Pattern: Fabric pattern is irregular. * **Equalize ** Adjust the value to equalize the difference in brightness caused by crease in the fabric. ※ Note: Depending on the fabric, some colors or patterns may be distorted. Refer to the attached image. below. ![seamless_1.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/13171432946713) * **Smooth ** When the connected part of the fabrics are not smooth by crease in the fabric, align weave areas equally. ![image-20221201-064052.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/13171781957657) * **Show/Hide Grid ** Click Show/Hide icon in Preview window at the bottom to check the grid of the repeated texture. **Save Texture Image** 1. Click Save at the bottom to save the generated texture as Image file. → Save Textures window appears. 2. Select the textures and map type to save and click OK button. → Each map name is automatically applied after the set name and saved as PNG files. **Apply Texture** 1. When the texture generating is complete, click the Apply & Close button at the bottom right of Texture Generator. → The texture is applied to the fabric simultaneously and the Texture generator is closed.
content_description: Create and manipulate seamless texture maps from scanned images, allowing for real-time visualization and application within a 3D environment.

title: Express Silk, Velvet and Glass Materials
content: **Express Silk, Velvet and Glass Materials** Express Silk, Velvet and Glass Materials Express Silk Express Velvet Express Glass **Express Silk, Velvet and Glass Materials** \- Express fabric or other objects as silk, velvet, and glass. \- Object Browser ▶ Fabric ▶ Property Editor ▶ Material ▶ **Type**. **Express Silk** \- Select the object to be edited in the Object Browser. \- In the Property Editor ▶ Material ▶ **Type** , select Fabric_Silk/Satin. \- The selected object is expressed in silk material in the 3D window. **Express Velvet** \- Select the object to be edited in the Object Browser. \- In the Property Editor ▶ Material ▶ **Type** , select Fabric_Velvet. \- The selected object is expressed in velvet material in the 3D window. **Express Glass** \- Select the object to be edited in the Object Browser. \- In the Property Editor ▶ Material ▶ **Type** , select Glass. \- The selected object is expressed in glass material in the 3D window. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: Explore how to easily express objects in silk, velvet, and glass materials using our intuitive Object Browser and Property Editor tools.

title: glTF a Standard Fabric File Compatibility (ver 6.1)
content: **List of Contents** **Export ** **Import** ### Objective Import or export PBR material and the CLO's physical property as a glTF file. ### Operation **Export** 1. Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Export ▶ Click Fabric (GLTF/GLB) menu. → Save File window appears. 2. Set the file saving path and name then click OK. → Export gLTF window appears. 3. Set the fabric you want to export and format then click OK. → The selected fabric is exported as a glTF or GLB file. **※ Note:** * Object Browser ▶ Fabric Tab ▶ You can also right-click on fabric items and **Export (GLTF/GLB)** menu. * It's not possible to export the fabric with Substance (SBSAR) material due to the license issue. **Import** 1. Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ Click GLTF / GLB menu. or drag and drop the file in the 3D / 2D window. → Import window appears. 2. Change the type of object to **Fabric** and click OK. → Import Fabric window appears. 3. Select the desired fabric and click OK. → The fabric is added to the Fabric Tab in the Object Browser. **※ Note:** You can also drag and drop a GLTF/GLB file in the fabric item or the fabric tab in the Object Browser. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for importing and exporting PBR materials and CLO's physical properties as glTF or GLB files.

title: Internal Rectangle
content: **List of Contents** Internal Rectangle Create **Internal Rectangle ** \- Create a rectangle within a Pattern. \- Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Create ▶ **Internal Rectangle** \- 2D Toolbar ▶ ![Toolbar_2D_Shape_Inner_Square.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001215267/Toolbar_2D_Shape_Inner_Square.png)**Internal Rectangle** **Create** * **Create**** ** \- Click and drag within a Pattern to create a rectangle in the 2D window. \- To create a square, hold down the Shift key from the keyboard while click and drag. * **Create with Specific Values** \- Click within a Pattern to create an Internal Rectangle with specific values. \- The Create Rectangle window appears. * Size Set width and height of the Internal Rectangle. * Replicate Interval : Set the distance between each replicated rectangles. Angle : Set the angle between each replicated rectangles. Number of Shapes : Set the number of rectangles to be replicated. * Position Outline : Configure the rectangle’s location by setting the its outline’s offset from the Pattern outlines’ left, right, top, and bottom. Center : Configure the rectangle’s location by setting the its center’s offset from the Pattern outlines’ left, right, top, and bottom. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on how to create and customize internal rectangles within a pattern using the 2D design tools.

title: How long will it take me to learn CLO?
content: **Question** How long will it take me to learn CLO? **Answer** The learning pace for CLO software differs for each individual and depends on the hours of practice and the complexity of your project. Therefore, it is hard to estimate the learning period, but everyone can reach a professional level after a certain practice. Some CLO users get it quickly through online tutorials on various channels and communicating with other CLO users via [CLO community forum](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/community/topics). If you could build your network, you may be able to acquire more extensive knowledge than others. For more information, please refer to the article about the [Available Training Resources](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115013367088).
content_description: Discover how individual practice and community resources can influence your learning journey with CLO software.

title: Substance
content: **Set the file format as Substance at the right menu of Material, you can use SBSAR file of Substance which is the main application of physical based rendering.** #### 1. Click a fabric in ![Fabric Tab.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/38101422930457) **Fabric** tab in [Object Browser](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/ko/articles/115000374247-%EB%AC%BC%EC%B2%B4%EC%B0%BD-Object-Browser-). 2. title: Displacement Map (ver5.1.0)
content: ### ** Objective ** Express thickness or bumpiness of fabrics or textures. Applied result can be only checked in the [Render](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/sections/115003861567-V-Ray-%EB%A0%8C%EB%8D%94) window. ### **Location** Object Browser ▶ Fabric Tab ▶ Fabric (Select from the Fabric List) ▶ Property Editor ▶ Material ▶**Displacement Map** ### **Operation** 1. Follow the indicated path below: 2. Click the ![__.jpg](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360039757274) **Browse** button to add a displacement map and modify below settings as needed. ** Displacement Map ** | As displacement maps are grey-scaled, their height is determined by the level of darkness of the grey color. **📝****Note:** Increase the image resolution and apply the Gaussian Blur effect to express the texture smoothly. ![Displacement_Map_tip.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360042515013) ---|--- ** Amount ** | Adjust the maximum height of the displacement map. The white area of the displacement map shows the maximum height. e.g.) When the Amount is set to 10mm, the height for each color differs as below: White 10mm, Grey 5mm, Black 0mm ![Displacement_Map_Amount.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360041673514) ** Clipping ** | Adjust to delete all geometries below the Clipping value. e.g.) When you want to delete geometries of the certain area: ![Displacement_Map_Clipping.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360041673574) **Particle Distance** | Adjust the Particle Distance of newly created meshes. **📝****Note** As more memory is used for lower Particle Distance, it is recommended not to set the Particle Distance below 1 for a wide area. ![Displacement_Map_Particle_Distance.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360042512993) **Keep Continuity** | Extend the adjacent face to eliminate the boundary line. **📝****Note:** Only applicable to Welded OBJs. ![unnamed.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360042513033)
content_description: This webpage provides detailed instructions on how to apply and adjust displacement maps in fabric textures to accurately express their thickness and bumpiness in a 3D modeling environment.

title: Custom Resolution Setting
content: ### **Objective** Set partially set Patterns as custom resolutions (ver2.5.0). **Location** 3D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005596727/56165.PNG) **Custom Resolution** Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ **Custom Resolution** ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below:** **3D Toolbar ▶![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005596727/56165.PNG) **Custom Resolution** **Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ Custom Resolution** → Custom Resolution window appears. 2. Click **Add Custom Resolution** at the top-right corner of the window. → Current Garment resolution settings is now being applied and saved in the list. → Items below are being included. a. **Particle Distance** for each Pattern b. **Add'l Thickness - Collision** for each Pattern c. **Avatar Skin Offset** d. **Simulation Quality** 3. To go back to previously saved Custom Resolution status while modifying a Garment, double-click on the saved Custom Resolution from the list. → The Custom Resolution is now being changed.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for setting and managing custom resolutions for patterns in Clo3D's 3D Toolbar and Main Menu.

title: Create Binding
content: **Create Binding** \- Easily create Binding along Pattern outlines. ** ** \- Select the ![binding.jpg](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001829127/binding.jpg)**Binding** tool from the 3D toolbar. \- Pattern outlines where Binding can be created appear in dashed lines. \- Click to start and double click to finish the selection. \- The Binding is created along the selected Pattern outline and its properties appear in the Property Editor.
content_description: This web page provides a straightforward guide for users to easily create Binding along Pattern outlines using the Binding tool in the 3D toolbar.

title: Run V-Ray Render
content: ### **Objective** V-Ray Render produces more vivid and sophisticated images with clear seamlines and puckerings. **Location ** Main Menu ▶ Render ▶ **Render ** Main Menu ▶ Display ▶ Window ▶ **Render** ** Operation** 1. Select the too/menu indicated in Location. → The Render window appears. 2. Click on the ![interactive_render.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115025949628) **Interactive Render** tool from the Render toolbar or click on the following direction,"Click here to start the Interactive Render," at the center of the Render window to start the real time render. → The 3D Garment and Avatar in the 3D window are rendered in real time, reflecting the [3D view](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/sections/115000628267-%EB%B7%B0-%EC%A0%9C%EC%96%B4). → Any changes made to material properties are applied to the Render window in real-time when the Interactive Render is active. **📝****Note: • **When the **![Camera Lock On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/33940373641753)Lock Camera** in the Render toolbar is activated, tthe render view remains fixed while controlling the view in the 3D window. (ver 2024.1) • At the bottom left of the render window, you can adjust the size of the interactive render screen. 3. To temporarily stop the render, select the ![stop_render.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115025910647) **Stop Render** tool from the Render toolbar. → The render stops temporarily. 4. To restart the render, please select the ![interactive_render.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115025949628) **Interactive Render** tool again. Or, to finish the render and extract the rendered image, click on the ![final_render.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115025910747) **Final Render (Image/ Video)** tool. → The final render image is saved according to the [render properties](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115014899148)**,[ light properties](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115014899168), **and **[image/ video properties](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115014785207)**.
content_description: Discover how to utilize V-Ray Render for creating stunning, high-quality images with seamless details in real-time using the Interactive Render tool.
